subject: Bancorp: Redwood eval plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@bancorp.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@bancorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Bancorp: Redwood eval plan & next steps

Hi Emma / Alex,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the thoughtful discussion. Below is a concise recap and the proposed Redwood eval plan so your team can get a benchmark for model fit and quality regressions.

Recap / priorities
- Goal: Replace rule-based customer responses in billing workflows and reduce manual review by 40% while keeping risky responses flagged for human review.
- Success metrics: accuracy on labeled prompts (exact/partial match), semantic similarity to gold responses, and safety/PII leakage checks.
- Hard constraint: budgeted inference cost target ~$0.005 per 1k tokens for production path.

Recommended models to evaluate (prioritized)
1) meta/llama-2-13b-chat-q4: good baseline for chat-style instructions
2) redwood/v1-8b-chat-quant: strong cost/latency perf for high throughput
3) open/juliet-3b-instruct: lighter-weight baseline for constrained replies

Proposed eval setup on Redwood
- Dataset format: CSV with columns [id, input, expected_response, category, severity, notes]. We attached a 100-row sample (bancorp-sample-queries.csv).
- Prompt sets: include 3 buckets — billing-clarity, payment-errors, escalation-handling. We’ll provide example prompts and expected responses.
- Scoring criteria: (a) automated exact/partial match; (b) token-overlap F1; (c) semantic similarity using redwood-embed-2 embeddings with cosine threshold 0.75; (d) safety flags + manual spot-checks.
- Runbook: create an eval job in Redwood Console or via API (we can create the project for you). Typical run takes 24-72h depending on candidate models.

Next steps / asks
1) Please confirm (A) the three prompt buckets above and (B) whether we can use the provided sample as representative.
2) If yes, please upload a 1-2k row CSV to the S3 link I’ll provide (or I can open a temporary project and upload for you).
3) Redwood will run an initial smoke test across the three candidate models, send a report with per-prompt failure cases, and propose a canary configuration for Dedicated or Hosted routing.

Attachments: redwood-eval-spec-v1.pdf (eval spec + scoring config), bancorp-sample-queries.csv (sample rows)

Timeline: If you can confirm and share sample by next Tue (2026-03-02), we can deliver the first report by 2026-03-06.

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if useful - available Wed morning PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Office: +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa - thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick clarifications before we upload: 

1) For the semantic similarity threshold you suggested (0.75) - is that per-prompt or averaged across the bucket? Would you recommend a different threshold for high-severity prompts (e.g., escalations)?
2) On safety flags / PII checks, can you confirm what Redwood flags out of the box vs. what requires a custom rule set?

We like the candidate model list but want some guidance on expected latency for redwood/v1-8b-chat-quant at our average payload (approx 250 tokens). Also, for cost modeling, could you share a quick estimate for 100k monthly calls across the three candidate models?

We’ll prepare a 200-row sample export and aim to upload by EOD Fri. Could you post the S3/upload link?

Thanks - Emma

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Bancorp: Redwood eval plan & next steps

Hi Emma - looping in a couple of technical details from the infra side.

Short answers to your questions:
- Semantic threshold: we recommend per-prompt thresholds. For standard billing/clarity prompts, 0.75 cosine on redwood-embed-2 is a good starting point; for high-severity escalation prompts, raise to 0.80-0.85 and include a manual review if below threshold.
- Safety/PII checks: Redwood has built-in heuristic detectors (PII regex, out-of-domain trigger warnings) and an opt-in ML classifier for sensitive content. Custom rules (e.g., company-specific account-number patterns) are trivial to add to the eval pipeline - we can take a small rule set you provide and run it during evaluation.
- Latency: redwood/v1-8b-chat-quant at ~250 tokens median payload should be ~120-180ms p95 on Dedicated GPU pool; hosted may vary depending on tenancy.
- Cost: rough back-of-envelope: for 100k monthly calls (avg 250 tokens) - redwood/v1-8b-quant ~ $X (we'll generate precise pricing breakdown in the report).

Operational notes for upload and run
1) We can create a temporary eval project in your preferred region (us-east-1). If you prefer S3, upload the CSV to the bucket we’ll provision. Otherwise, you can share a Drive link and we’ll ingest.
2) Scoring config: we’ll produce a CSV report with per-id scoring columns (exact_match, f1, cosine_sim, safety_flag) and a summary dashboard with per-prompt failure examples.
3) Outputs: we can include the top-K model candidates, per-prompt latency, and a regression alert if model output semantic similarity drops > 10% vs baseline.

I’ve attached a short eval spec for engineers and a sample python snippet to compute cosine similarity using redwood-embed-2. If you’d like, we’ll also run a short smoke test on a 50-row subset first.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
